scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Slam the brakes hard, and older cars could skid straight ahead. With ABS, you can still steer. How?

scenes.name: lock
scenes.text: If a wheel stops spinning while the car is still moving, it skids. A skidding tyre has less grip, and you can't steer.

scenes.name: sensors
scenes.text: Each wheel has a speed sensor. A control unit watches all of them, many times a second.

scenes.name: detect
scenes.text: If one wheel slows down much faster than the car, the computer knows it's about to lock.

scenes.name: pulse
scenes.text: A valve block releases and reapplies brake pressure on that wheel, many times a second, keeping it right at the edge of grip.

scenes.name: steer
scenes.text: Because the wheels keep rolling, you can steer around an obstacle. The pedal may buzz under your foot. That's normal, keep pressing firmly.

scenes.name: india
scenes.text: ABS is now standard on new cars, and since 2019, it's required on motorcycles above one hundred and twenty five cc.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Sense, release, reapply, steer. Braking without skidding. Follow for more on how things really work.
